$comment: The ONE authority for which documents a source area owes. Registry: docs-sync/source-doc-mapping, docs-sync/coupled-surface-inventory, docs-sync/same-change-enforcement. Before this file existed the repo had exactly one declared coupling (registry.ts -> STORE_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH.md) and 69 documents nobody could attribute to anything. Read by scripts/doc-coupling.mjs and by nothing else -- a map without a reader is a good intention in a syntax that parses.

surfaceTypes.reference: The implemented-product contract a developer reads. REQUIRED on every entry. Satisfied only by the exact path named -- never by any file under docs/, because a prefix-shaped satisfaction is most cheaply discharged by accident.
surfaceTypes.generatedBy: Optional. When the reference doc is DERIVED from the source, name the generator. A derived doc is checked by recomputation (its own --check), not by this map's same-change nag, so declaring it here suppresses a nag the generator already answers better.
surfaceTypes.note: Optional prose stating this entry's DISMISSAL ALTITUDE -- what level of change reaches this surface. Written into the map so dismissal is a documented policy applied per change rather than a judgment call repeated per change.

derivation.$comment: Where a naming convention couples source to doc MECHANICALLY, derive the pair and let the map hold only exceptions -- the convention IS the recomputation, and a derived coupling is self-repairing under rename, which is a declared map's characteristic death. This repo has exactly one such convention.

colocatedReadme.rule: A README.md inside a source directory D is coupled to every source file directly under D and its subdirectories, excluding subdirectories that carry a README.md of their own (the nearest README wins, so a change is never nagged about a grandparent's doc).

coverage.$comment: The map is the real gate: COVERAGE, not membership. Validating that every path a map names resolves on disk is structurally incapable of seeing what the map omits. `areaRoots` enumerates the coupling universe; every directory it yields must be claimed by an entry, by a derived colocated README, or by `unmappedAllowlist` with a reason. The residue is counted and held by the ratchet (bucket docs:unmappedAreas), because 40-odd unmapped areas is not a number anyone drives to zero this week -- what the bucket buys is that the next one is refused.

unmappedAllowlist.src/types: Generated and hand-written type declarations. Types are the contract; a prose doc restating them would be the second place the same fact is stated.
unmappedAllowlist.src/components/icons: Icon components. No behaviour to describe.
unmappedAllowlist.src/components/illustrations: Static illustration components. No behaviour to describe.
unmappedAllowlist.src/lib/constants: Constant tables. The values are the documentation.

entries.note: DERIVED. Any change to the manifest reaches this surface; the generator's --check enforces it byte-for-byte, which is stronger than a same-change nag, so this entry is declared but not nagged.
Adding, deleting or re-pointing a store reaches this surface -- the doc states the store COUNT and the edges. An internal change to a store's action bodies does not.
That document carries a coverage table and a 'Not covered' table. Adding, deleting or skipping a spec reaches both. A locator change inside an existing test does not.

The fixture set is the suite's PRECONDITION, and that document states what a seeded database contains — list titles, item counts, how many are ranked. Changing the fixture inventory reaches it. Changing a diagnostic message does not.
This document carries two dated corrections because it drifted from its source twice. Any change to which rung of the ladder is WIRED reaches it. Threshold tuning inside a wired rung does not.
A prop or layout-variant change reaches this surface; the document enumerates both.

DELIBERATELY EMPTY source set, and the reason is the finding: every file this document names (src/app/features/matching/components/SwipeableCard.tsx, ParticleThemeSettings.tsx) is absent, and the identifiers ParticleTheme / particleTheme / PARTICLE_THEMES have zero occurrences anywhere in src/. It is a design for an unbuilt feature. Recorded here with `sourceStatus: unimplemented` so the stale-glob check does not fail on it and the next reader is not left to rediscover it; the document itself carries the dated correction.

DERIVED. The 63 report files are the authority for what was found; the ledger holds identity, state and probes. Editing a report re-derives the finding's key, so `npm run findings:check` fails until the ledger is re-ingested — which is stronger than a same-change nag, so this entry is declared but not nagged.
A change to the status vocabulary, the grounding clause forms or the stop-condition semantics reaches the backlog's own header, which states all three. A message-wording change does not.
A change to the state vocabulary, the identity function or the probe semantics reaches the ledger's own header, which states all three. A message-wording change does not.
The manifest maps capabilities to COMMANDS. Renaming, adding or deleting a script reaches it -- that is precisely how `lint` sat pointing at a command Next 16 had removed. A dependency bump does not.
CLAUDE.md is the agent-facing orientation. A change to how the repo is BUILT, LINTED or TESTED reaches it. Feature work does not.
A new counter needs a bucket in the same change, or it measures nothing. A message-wording change does not.
This file and its reader are each other's coupled surface: a new check needs its configuration declared in the same change.

crossRepoSurfaces.$comment: Reported, never gated. A check whose outcome is a function of whether a sibling checkout exists at some relative path is present on the author's box and absent on every fresh clone and every runner.
